facts.advisory_summary:
actix-files has a possible exposure of information vulnerability — ### Summary

When passing a non-existing folder to the `actix_files::Files::new()` method causes the actix server to expose unexpected files.

### Details

The `actix-files` library exposes a [`Files` struct](https://github.com/actix/actix-web/blob/fba766b4beb92278665d58815c94d336015225c5/actix-files/src/files.rs#L38) that configures an actix `service` to serve the files in a folder as static assets. Below you can find the [signature of the `Files::new` method](https://github.com/actix/actix-web/blob/fba766b4beb92278665d58815c9

expect.note: Only Files::new call is src/actix/web_ui.rs:43, and web_ui_folder() (web_ui.rs:22-29) returns None unless static_content_dir exists and is a directory, so Files::new is never given a non-existent folder (the advisory's precondition). NamedFile use in lib/collection/src/common/snapshot_stream.rs:50 is not Files.

facts.advisory_summary:
[actix-files] Panic triggered by empty Range header in GET request for static file — ### Summary
A GET request for a static file served by `actix-files` with an empty `Range` header triggers a panic. With `panic = "abort"`, a remote user may crash the process on-demand.

### Details
`actix-files` assumes that `HttpRange::parse()`, when `Ok`, always returns a vector with at least one element. When `parse()` is called on an empty string, it returns `Ok(vec![])`. This can cause a panic at named.rs:534 when handling an HTTP request with an empty `Range:` header. This shouldn't significantly impact

expect.note: actix-files 0.6.6 named.rs:533-535 does HttpRange::parse(..) then ranges[0] unguarded; range.rs parse returns Ok(vec![]) for empty header. NamedFile responder serves the web UI (src/actix/web_ui.rs:43, /dashboard enabled by default, static dir shipped in image, whitelisted from api-key auth) and snapshot downloads (lib/collection/src/common/snapshot_stream.rs:50). Unauthenticated GET /dashboard/index.html with empty Range header hits the panic (release profile is unwind, so it kills the request/worker rather than the process).

facts.advisory_summary:
actix-http has HTTP/1.1 CL.TE Request Smuggling  — A vulnerability in `actix-http`'s HTTP/1.1 request parser allows an unauthenticated remote client to smuggle requests in deployments where a front-end HTTP intermediary and the Actix backend disagree about whether `Content-Length` or `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` defines the request body length.

## Severity

**Medium**.
This is an HTTP request smuggling vulnerability that can be triggered over the network without application-level credentials. Exploitation requires a specific proxy topology: an upstream proxy, WAF, load balancer, or similar in

expect.note: actix-http 3.7.0 is the HTTP/1 server under actix-web 4.9 (Cargo.toml actix-web dep; REST API on 6333). Every inbound request goes through its h1 decoder, so the CL/TE parsing is exercised by attacker requests. Exploitation needs a front-end proxy that disagrees on CL vs TE (common for internet-facing deployments behind an LB/ingress).

No anyhow::Error::downcast_mut call in app: only downcast_mut is lib/common/issues/src/typemap.rs:27 on Box<dyn Any>. Other anyhow users in deployed closure (storage, dataset, qdrant main/consensus) use context/?, no downcast_mut; lindera* users are behind off multiling features.

facts.advisory_summary:
bytes has integer overflow in BytesMut::reserve — # Details

In the unique reclaim path of `BytesMut::reserve`, the condition
```rs
if v_capacity >= new_cap + offset
```
uses an unchecked addition. When `new_cap + offset` overflows `usize` in release builds, this condition may incorrectly pass, causing `self.cap` to be set to a value that exceeds the actual allocated capacity. Subsequent APIs such as `spare_capacity_mut()` then trust this corrupted `cap` value and may create out-of-bounds slices, leading to UB.

This behavior is observable in release builds (integer overflow wraps), whereas de

expect.note: bytes 1.9.0 is everywhere (actix-http, h2, hyper, tonic) but the bug needs BytesMut::reserve with new_cap+offset overflowing usize. Reserve calls on network paths are bounded (actix-http h1/mod.rs:61, dispatcher.rs:989 fixed HW sizes; tonic codec/decode.rs:190 len from 4-byte gRPC header <=4GiB; h2 hpack decoder.rs:528 bounded by header-list limits); no caller passes an attacker-chosen near-usize::MAX additional, which would otherwise hit capacity-overflow anyway. facts.advisory_summary:
`let_cxx_string!` uses uninitialized value due to exception safety violations — In affected versions of this crate, `let_cxx_string!` is not exception safe. After creating the `StackString`, if `match $value` panics, the content of `StackString` is not yet initialized, while the drop implementation of `StackString` unconditionally deinitializes the content, leading to use of uninitialized value.

The soundness issue was fixed in version `1.0.195` by moving drop logics to separate drop guard after initializing the `StackString`.

Double free in `DCtx::try_clone` — `DCtx::try_clone` (`experimental` feature, deprecated) is a plain copy of the
C context. A context owning a dictionary (from `load_dictionary`,
`ref_prefix` or `init_using_dict`) or a dictionary table (`ref_ddict` with
`RefMultipleDDicts`) ended up with both copies freeing it. A context cloned
mid-frame resumed on uninitialized stream state. The clone also silently lost
the `WindowLogMax` limit.

The flaw was corrected by refusing to clone such contexts, and by carrying
over the parameters the copy leaves out.

expect.note: DCtx::try_clone is behind the 'experimental' feature, which is off (zstd 0.13 default features only); actix-http never clones contexts.
